Instruction tuning (IT) helps to align large language models (LLMs) with users expectations so that LLMs are capable of understanding user queries and generating helpful, comprehensive and focused responses without few-shot examples.
outputs: The paper focuses on instruction-following generation, where models generate responses to diverse user instructions in multiple languages, evaluated on helpfulness, fluency, factuality, and other dimensions.

We also introduce lightweight surface metrics: language correctness, spellcheck correctness, and relevance to the task (how often responses are relevant to their tasks, evaluated using LLama-2-chat-7B).

We also introduce lightweight surface metrics: language correctness (how often the language of the response matches the language of the task), spellcheck correctness (which portion of words in the responses pass spell checking), and relevance to the task (how often responses are relevant to their tasks, evaluated using LLama-2-chat-7B).

guideline: Evaluators scored responses on six criteria on a scale from 0 to 2: helpfulness, language correctness, fluency, factual accuracy, logical coherence, and harmlessness.
Evaluators are provided with an evaluation instruction describing six criteria (helpfulness, language correctness, fluency, factual accuracy, logical coherence, harmlessness) and scoring guidelines.

Evaluators are provided with the evaluation instruction which describes 6 evaluation criteria and requirements for each of the {0, 1, 2} scores. Importantly, the instruction provides a detailed description on the helpfulness and Accuracy scores, to reduce ambiguity in their interpretation which can happen given the high diversity of evaluation tasks.
